svg.title: compose-new-comment · long · 160x48
svg.text: Agreed, and I think the README should say so explicitly. Here's what I'd add under Keys:
- `j` / `k` move one line and stop at either end of the file; they never wrap around.
- `G` jumps to the last line and `g` to the first.
- `J` / `K` move by hunk, and stop at the first and the last hunk.
I also checked the three cases you listed against the current build. All three behave as
described, so I don't think we need a code change here, just the docs. If you want, I can
open a follow-up for the wrap-around idea, since a few people asked for it in the
discussion, but I'd keep it behind a setting so the default stays the same as today.
One more thing: the help panel lists `j` as "Line down" but the footer says "Down". We
should pick one. I'd go with the help panel's wording because it's more specific, and the
he defaults when it is empty,
footer has room for it at 100 columns.
1. Open a file longer than the screen
4. Press `J` and `K` on a file with three hunks
Every one of them stopped where the docs will say it stops. The only surprise was `K` on
the first hunk, which does nothing rather than wrapping to the last one, and that matches
Finally, the screenshot in the README is from 0.5 and still shows the old title bar. I'll
refresh it in the same PR, and add one of the diff view with a cursor on a hunk header,
since that's the part people ask about.
A few notes for whoever picks up the wrap-around follow-up:
- keep the default as it is today
- put the setting next to the other viewer settings
- make `G` and `g` respect it too, so the keys stay consistent
- add a snapshot for the wrapped position at both widths
I'll link this thread from the follow-up so the context isn't lost. If anything in the
list above looks wrong, say so here and I'll fix it before the PR goes up.
Thanks again for the careful report. The steps made this quick to check.
